detail.abstract:
Background: Respiratory diseases accounted for three of the top five causes of deaths globally in 2021. Research is crucial to understanding disease determinants, effects of interventions, and to improving patient outcomes. We analysed global patterns and temporal trends for public and philanthropic investments, research collaborations and publications for respiratory research. 

Methods: We searched Digital Science Dimensions database for respiratory disease-related research funding awards between Jan 1, 2000, and Dec 31, 2023. We combined human expert input with a novel automated framework based on machine learning and large language models to categorise funding awards by respiratory disease type (e.g. acute infection, airways, lung cancer), priority research theme (e.g. vaccine, climate threats, antimicrobial resistance), and research phase (e.g. preclinical, phase 1-4 trials, public health). Funding amount was compared with the global burden of specific conditions, measured by disability-adjusted life-years using data from the Global Burden of Disease study. We analysed co-authorship networks of countries, showing the evolution of research collaboration over time. 

Findings: We identified 73,093 awards totaling $69.6bn in 2000 to 2023. Preclinical research received $51.9 bn (74.6% of total funding), phase 1-4 trials $5.7bn (8.3%) and public health $8.3bn (11.9%). The most funded respiratory disease type was acute infection ($32.1 bn, 46.1%), followed by airway diseases ($14.4bn, 20.7%), and lung cancer ($8.8bn, 12.6%). Analysis by priority theme revealed $17.3bn allocated to vaccination research (24.8%), with low levels of investment into research on climate threats ($1.1bn, 1.6%), antimicrobial resistance ($0.6bn, 0.8%) and pandemic preparedness ($0.4bn, 0.6%).  By funding received per associated respiratory DALY, high-income countries received $61/DALY whereas low-income countries $0.016/DALY. Respiratory infection received more than $15/DALY while non-infection less than $10/DALY in 2019-2020, reversing the trend of prior two decades.  Network analysis revealed that collaboration intensity peaks roughly three years after  funding injections in the years of global respiratory events. The collaboration network of co-authorship is characterised by a rigid core of high-income countries and a flexible periphery of low- and middle-income countries through time. 

Interpretation: There is inequity between rich and poor countries in the current respiratory disease funding landscape. Rich countries have been consistently central to global research collaboration, with widening yet volatile involvement of poor countries over time. The current funding landscape is not obviously well prepared for current and future respiratory threats such as antimicrobial resistance, climate change and future pandemics. Long-term investment can build sustainable research networks with more equitable and efficient allocation of funds.

detail.abstract:
Background: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) with large vessel occlusion (LVO) carries high morbidity despite endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).Symptomatic hemorrhagic transformation (sHT), a reperfusion-related complication, remains a critical concern. Elevated blood pressure variability (BPV) post-EVT correlates with sHT risk, but traditional BPV assessments lack real-time utility. We propose a machine learning model analyzing continuous blood pressure and heart rate to predict sHT early, enabling timely intervention and improved outcomes.

Methods: We conducted a retrospective study including 615 patients with AIS who achieved successful recanalization after EVT across two hospitals. Blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) measurements were recorded at 30-minute or 1-hour intervals during the first 24 hours post-EVT, and non-contrast head CT was performed to determine the presence of sHT. Patients were categorized into symptomatic HT (sHT) and non-sHT groups based on CT findings. We applied deep learning models, including LeNet and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), to characterize and compare BP/HR temporal patterns between groups. GAN-based augmentation was used to mitigate class imbalance by generating synthetic sHT cases, and a sliding-window strategy was implemented to support real-time prediction of sHT.

Results: Using data from two hospitals, the deep learning framework identified distinct pre-sHT temporal signatures in systolic (SBP), diastolic (DBP), and HR, with SBP exhibiting the largest and most informative fluctuations prior to sHT onset. After GAN-based augmentation to address class imbalance, the model achieved strong discrimination for sHT prediction in both the training and held-out test evaluations. In the independent external validation cohort, the model correctly identified all 73 non-sHT cases and 25 of 28 sHT cases, yielding an AUC of 0.978, an accuracy of 97.0%, a specificity of 100%, and a sensitivity of 89.3%. With a 10-point sliding window, the model provided near–real-time forecasting of sHT in the next measurement interval with high accuracy. Notably, the optimal decision threshold was not identical across hospitals, consistent with inter-site differences in baseline haemodynamics, measurement frequency, and case mix. Therefore, the operating threshold was optimized separately for each hospital on the corresponding test/evaluation cohort using ROC analysis and Youden’s J statistic to balance sensitivity and specificity. In the overall test set, the model showed good generalization, achieving high accuracy in the non-sHT group and substantially improved performance for sHT following GAN-based balancing.

Conclusion: Our findings show that deep learning models can anticipate symptomatic haemorrhagic transformation after EVT using early post-procedural blood pressure and heart-rate trajectories. In this framework, LeNet was used for prediction, while a GANs was applied separately to mitigate class imbalance through synthetic case generation. The resulting pipeline supports near–real-time risk estimation with high discriminative performance, offering a clinically actionable strategy for earlier identification of high-risk patients and timely intervention, with operating thresholds calibrated to the intended deployment setting.

detail.abstract:
Background: Deep learning enabled automated tumor segmentation on whole-body PET/CT, but robustness remains challenged by heterogeneous tracer uptake, anatomical variability, and inter-center differences. The fourth autoPET challenge introduced an interactive segmentation paradigm using incremental simulated user prompts, combining automated efficiency with expert oversight.

Methods: Two tasks were open to international challenge contestants. Task 1 promoted interactive lesion segmentation on whole-body PET/CT using progressively simulated user clicks over multiple interaction steps. Task 2 addressed longitudinal lesion segmentation on whole-body CT, leveraging paired baseline and follow-up scans with provided lesion center information to model temporal consistency. Models were trained and evaluated on expert-annotated datasets (FDG & PSMA PET/CT for Task 1 and paired CT scans for Task 2), using pre-simulated human interactions. Performance was assessed using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), False Positive Volume (FPV), False Negative Volume (FNV), and area-under-curve across interaction steps. Task 1 included ∼30,000 training and ∼3,000 test lesions, while Task 2 comprised ∼7,500 training and ∼4,500 test lesions.

Findings: In Task 1, interactive methods improved progressively with increasing interactions. The top model achieved a mean DSC=0·74, FNV=2·17ml, and FPV=1·30ml. Human-in-the-loop refinement consistently reduced false negatives but modestly increased false positives, especially for small or low-contrast lesions. Leading methods remained robust (mean DSC>0·64) across centers and tracers, and ensemble voting outperformed individual submissions. Task 2 proved substantially harder, with a best mean DSC=0·38. Temporal priors helped but were insufficient to capture lesion regression, disappearance, or emergence.

Interpretations: Interactive segmentation outperforms fully autonomous approaches and shows promise for reducing expert workload while preserving clinical sensitivity. However, challenges persist for small lesions, high physiological uptake regions, and longitudinal tracking. The findings support the integration of human-in-the-loop strategies into clinical workflows while underscoring the need for domain-robust methods and improved temporal modeling in routine deployment.​

title: THE DARK SIDE OF HYPER-PERSONALIZATION: PRIVACY CALCULUS, ALGORITHMIC SURVEILLANCE PERCEPTIONS, AND CONSUMER BACKLASH IN DIGITAL ECOSYSTEMS

detail.title: THE DARK SIDE OF HYPER-PERSONALIZATION: PRIVACY CALCULUS, ALGORITHMIC SURVEILLANCE PERCEPTIONS, AND CONSUMER BACKLASH IN DIGITAL ECOSYSTEMS
detail.abstract: Contemporary digital marketing operates on an implicit assumption: more personalization generates more value. Drawing on privacy calculus theory, psychological reactance theory, and signaling theory, this study challenges that assumption by theorizing and empirically demonstrating a Personalization Toxicity Threshold (PTT) a curvilinear inflection point at which increasing personalization intensity transitions from value creation to perceived intrusion. Across three experimental studies (N = 1,847) conducted in GDPR-regulated and non-GDPR digital environments, the research demonstrates that (1) the personalization–brand equity relationship follows an inverted U-shape rather than a positive linear trajectory; (2) perceived algorithmic surveillance fully mediates the negative segment of this curve; and (3) consumer data literacy and product involvement moderate the precise location of the PTT inflection point. Structural equation modeling with latent interaction terms and quadratic specifications provides strong support for all hypotheses. The findings carry substantial implications for data-driven marketing strategy, challenging prevailing optimization frameworks that treat personalization depth as an unambiguously desirable parameter. The study contributes a replicable PTT measurement scale and a diagnostic tool for marketing managers to identify brand-specific personalization thresholds.

title: Access and Service Pricing on Innovation Platforms under Quality Competition with Information Asymmetry
affiliations: Wuhan University of Technology and Wuhan University of Technology

detail.title: Access and Service Pricing on Innovation Platforms under Quality Competition with Information Asymmetry
detail.abstract: Due to information asymmetry in the quality of research services, innovation platforms often face mismatches between supply and demand. As organizers of innovation ecosystems, platforms influence resource allocation efficiency by setting access fees on both sides, while resource providers determine service prices endogenously. This paper develops a three-party game-theoretic model of a two-sided innovation platform, where the platform sets access fees for both resource providers and users, while resource providers endogenously determine service prices. Providers are heterogeneous in service quality and cost, and users differ in their ability to discern quality. We examine how improvements in users’ information levels reshape the two-layer pricing structure—consisting of platform access fees and providers’ endogenous service prices—and thereby affect market outcomes. The results show that as users’ information levels improve, the platform reduces access fees on the provider side, while user-side pricing depends on the trade-off between demand elasticity and cross-side network effects. Changes in the two-layer pricing structure further amplify quality differentiation, driving the market from pooling equilibria under incomplete information to separating equilibria based on quality. High-quality providers obtain quality premiums, whereas low-quality providers experience declines in prices and profits. We further extend the baseline model by considering price signaling, government subsidies, and platform information upgrading. The extended results show that these mechanisms reinforce the role of information structure in shaping pricing and improve overall market efficiency and social welfare. Overall, the information environment plays a crucial role in shaping two-layer pricing, competition, and efficiency in innovation platforms.

title: The Agentic Frontier: Artificial Intelligence in Commercial Real Estate

detail.title: The Agentic Frontier: Artificial Intelligence in Commercial Real Estate
detail.abstract: We review the AI literature in commercial real estate through a framework linking four market frictions (opacity, search costs, illiquidity, and heterogeneity) to AI methods and testable market outcomes. The literature shows strong evidence that AI improves prediction, but almost none that better prediction reduces frictions or changes market outcomes. Adoption data from the Anthropic Economic Index, merged with occupational task profiles for 16 CRE occupations (324 tasks), show that AI usage divides along task type rather than task difficulty: information-processing tasks show high engagement regardless of importance, while tasks requiring physical presence or professional judgment show none. AI engages the highest-importance tasks in each occupation, not the most routine. A friction-by-method classification of 66 papers shows that half the cells are empty. The high-importance tasks at zero AI penetration define the "Agentic Frontier."

title: Siliconwashing: How Claims of AI Autonomy Hide the Blood and Sweat of Invisible Workers

detail.title: Siliconwashing: How Claims of AI Autonomy Hide the Blood and Sweat of Invisible Workers

publicationDetails.detailsText: X Congresso Internacional de Direitos Humanos de Coimbra, v. 10 n. 1 (2025)

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the term "siliconwashing", signifying the corporate practice of deploying narratives of AI autonomy to obscure the exploited human labor underpinning AI systems. We demonstrate how siliconwashing operates as the dialectical counterpart to "humanwashing": while humanwashing anthropomorphizes machines to exaggerate their capabilities, siliconwashing dehumanizes workers to render their labor invisible. Through the OpenAI case study, where content moderators earned $1.50 per hour reviewing traumatic material while the company marketed ChatGPT as autonomous and self-learning, we reveal how autonomy narratives systematically hide workers' blood and sweat. This dual legitimation strategy, elevating machines to autonomous agents while reducing humans to expendable components, creates hierarchies of worthiness that render Global South labor exploitation structurally invisible. We argue that every claim of AI autonomy conceals a chain of invisible workers whose suffering makes the "autonomous" system possible.

title: A Retrospective Exploration of Medication Administration Errors in a Tertiary Hospital
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Singapore (NUS) - Singapore General Hospital, University of Connecticut and National University of Singapore (NUS) - Singapore General Hospital

detail.title: A Retrospective Exploration of Medication Administration Errors in a Tertiary Hospital
detail.abstract:
Background: Electronic health records (EHRs) and medication worklists were introduced to reduce medication errors. Yet, these technologies remain a significant concern in nursing medication administration. User interface (UI) design contributes to medication error risk, yet few studies have examined medication worklists from nurses’ perspectives in relation to UI design. 
Aim: This retrospective exploratory study examined EHR UI limitations on potential risk of nursing medication administration errors. 
Methods: The study team reviewed 229 medication-related incident reports at a tertiary hospital over one year. The team included adult inpatient medication administration errors where nurses' interaction with the EHR's UI may have contributed to the error. The study team used Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis, guided by Nielsen's ten usability heuristics. Descriptive statistics summarized incident report distribution across UI limitation themes. 
Results: The study team analyzed 98 incident reports. Four themes emerged: 1) suboptimal visual presentation (46.6%), 2) insufficient clinical decision support features (34.0%), 3) ease of overrides (11.7%), and 4) difficult information retrieval (7.7%). Suboptimal visual presentation involved misinterpreted color-coding and overlooked medication remarks. Insufficient clinical decision support involved missed critical information and over-reliance on automated scheduling. Ease of overrides allowed bypassing safety measures. Difficult information retrieval limited access to comprehensive medication information across systems. 
Conclusion: Medication errors may arise from mismatches between nurses’ expectations of EHR support and the cognitive work required by the interface. Workflow deviations may represent adaptive responses to suboptimal UI design, shaped by human-computer interaction complexities. These findings support evidence-based interface improvements to strengthen medication administration safety.

title: The Transmission of Trade Shocks in Digital Markets
affiliations: University of Maryland, College Park

detail.title: The Transmission of Trade Shocks in Digital Markets
detail.abstract: We study how trade shocks are transmitted in digital marketplaces. Using product-level data from Amazon, we examine the 2025 escalation of U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports and the accompanying rise in trade policy uncertainty. We show that these shocks operate not only through prices, but also through non-price product attributes and the platform's allocation of visibility. Retail pass-through is incomplete: sellers absorb part of the cost shock, while the post-tariff ranking environment becomes less favorable to costly products. A structural demand model decomposes the resulting change in consumer surplus into preference shifts, entry, exit, product attributes, and algorithmic allocation. Product turnover partly offsets losses from weaker attributes and reduced visibility, but the shock disproportionately displaces relatively expensive, lower-quality products.

detail.title:
Recursive State Normalization (RSN): A Fixed-Point Metrology and Digital Provenance Framework for Aerospace Additive Manufacturing 
Recursive Structural Refinement for High-Stress Aerospace Components
detail.abstract:
Additive manufacturing (AM) of aerospace components introduces complex microstructural defects—including porosity, grain boundary segregation, residual stress, and crystallographic anisotropy—that standard nondestructive evaluation (NDE) workflows cannot reliably characterize. To bridge this gap, we introduce Recursive State Normalization (RSN): a digital provenance and metrology architecture designed to stabilize and validate high-stress 3D-printed aerospace parts. The framework recursively processes Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) and Micro-CT data, utilizing Recursive Structural Refinement operators to drive defect-state divergence within admissible tolerances. This iterative loop continues until it reaches fixed-point convergence, logging every state transition to an immutable cryptographic ledger for complete data traceability.

​The architecture’s theoretical convergence horizon features a multidimensional complexity bounded at 10^{15} admissible state evaluations, establishing a rigorous upper topological manifold limit rather than adding to actual manufacturing runtime. Adversarial robustness simulations validate that the RSN framework maintains strict convergence stability despite EBSD indexing noise, Micro-CT reconstruction artifacts, synthetic voids, and grain boundary misorientation offsets. Ultimately, RSN offers a standards-compliant augmentation layer designed for direct integration into ASTM, SAE, FAA, and NIST-aligned additive manufacturing certification workflows.

detail.abstract: This study examines the effects of special economic zones (SEZs) on firm growth and the regional business environment in Viet Nam, highlighting their key role as a policy tool to attract foreign investors. Using detailed panel data from Viet Nam’s 63 provinces from 2006 to 2020 and instrumental variables (IV) estimations, this study provides new insights into how SEZs impact firm growth and several dimensions of economic governance. SEZs are found to play a dual role. Provinces with broader SEZ coverage experienced increases in employment, revenues, and the number of foreign-invested enterprises. In contrast, domestic private firms faced declines in both revenues and numbers. SEZ exposure had negative effects on several aspects of provincial economic governance including land access, transparency in policy-making, and informal charges. In addition, the approval of the first SEZ was also associated with increased prevalence of informal charges and preferential treatment of foreign-invested enterprises and other big companies, which may indicate heightened inefficiencies and rent-seeking concerns.

detail.title: Community-Based Farmer Coaching And Peer Support To Address Claims Issues In Pcic Ro Iii-A: Basis For Strategic Plan
detail.abstract: This study examined the causes of crop insurance claim denials among insured rice farmers and proposed a Community-Based Farmer Coaching and Peer Support Program for the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC) Regional Office III-A in Nueva Ecija. The study aimed to describe the farmers' profile, identify common reasons for claim denials, assess their awareness of insurance claims procedures and requirements, and evaluate the perceived effectiveness and implementation challenges of the proposed intervention. A descriptive research design was employed involving 200 insured rice farmers with denied claims and selected PCIC personnel. Data were collected using structured survey questionnaires and analysed through frequency counts, percentages, weighted means, and ranking. Findings revealed that most respondents were middle-aged male farmers with basic educational attainment and limited farming experience. Despite prior orientations on crop insurance, respondents generally exhibited low to moderate awareness of claims procedures, filing deadlines, policy coverage, and documentary requirements. The most common reasons for claim denial were late filing of claims, expired insurance coverage, damages not covered under policy provisions, and harvesting prior to claim submission. Results further indicated that most farmers experienced claim denial only once, suggesting that procedural errors often occurred during initial claims processing due to insufficient guidance. The proposed Community-Based Farmer Coaching and Peer Support Program was evaluated positively in terms of usefulness, accessibility, relevance, and potential to improve farmers' compliance with insurance requirements and understanding of claims procedures. Overall, the study concludes that localized, continuous, and peer-assisted coaching interventions may reduce preventable claim denials and enhance the efficiency of crop insurance claims processing among insured farmers.

detail.abstract: This paper addresses grade comparability across exam cohorts when assessors and item sets change from year to year. Ordinal item scores reflect a mixture of student ability, item difficulty, and assessor severity; separating these components requires linking assumptions rarely verified empirically. We fit a sequence of Bayesian cumulative logit models to item-level scores from nine cohorts of an undergraduate statistics course. The setting is fully observational with no cross-grading and only partial assessor overlap, so cross-cohort alignment relies on repeated content used as anchors and on shared assessors. Sequential model expansion guided by posterior predictive checks reveals that treating anchors as having fixed difficulty across cohorts is inconsistent with the data. A soft-linking formulation, where linked items share a baseline difficulty but admit cohort-specific deviations regularised toward zero, removes the systematic misfit without discarding anchor information. Approximate cross-validation confirms that each modelling step improves out-of-sample predictive accuracy. Student ability estimates are robust to anchor specification (pairwise correlations exceeding 0.996), whereas cohort location estimates shift materially, which is a finding with direct consequences for grading policy. detail.abstract: The study aims to measure the profitability of spice crops, their marketing channels, marketing efficiency, and price spread effects. The study was based on a field survey of 320 spice farmers of Haryana state in India carried out between 2020 and 2021. The authors presented analytical purposes, compound growth rate, cost-benefit ratio, marketing channels, marketing efficiency and price spread effect. The growth of area and production of spice crops is not very strong compared to the profitability of spice crops. Cost-benefit ratio shows that spice crops are more profitable than traditional crops for farmers. However, due to high cost of cultivation, volatile prices, and fear of crop failure, area under spices cultivation is very small. Price spread effect is very high in channel I and II. The majority of farmers adopted inefficient marketing channel (low price for producer and high price for consumer) due to lack of storage facility and weak financial health. The role of government is important for protecting the rights of producers as well as consumers. Mediators' role should be minimized by government policy in the marketing of spice crops in Haryana so that farmers can charge the right price for their spice crops.

title: The Privacy Subsidy in Glosten-Milgrom: Bid-Ask Spread and Welfare under Flip-Noise Direction Observation
affiliations: The Open University of Japan

detail.title: The Privacy Subsidy in Glosten-Milgrom: Bid-Ask Spread and Welfare under Flip-Noise Direction Observation
detail.abstract: We derive a closed-form bid-ask spread and welfare decomposition for the Glosten-Milgrom 1985 sequential-trading model when the market maker observes the trade direction perturbed by a binary flip channel of probability η-a natural information-theoretic model of privacy mechanisms acting on the direction signal. Under a committed Bayesian market-maker pricing rule, the equilibrium spread is µ(1-2η)∆, where µ is the informed-trader fraction and ∆ = vH-vL the value range. The welfare decomposition identifies a per-trade transfer µη∆ from the protocol's liquidity pool to traders-the privacy subsidy, mirroring the Gaussian-Kyle analog established in prior work. The result extends the privacy-subsidy concept from continuous Gaussian to discrete two-state microstructure, demonstrating robustness across both classical models. Primary application: MPC-based matching engines with ε-differentiallyprivate direction disclosure, where the engine prices on a noisy direction signal.

title: Agentic AI, Large Language Model Methodologies, and Workflow-Level ROI in Portfolio Risk Analysis at Navy Federal Credit Union: An Evidence-Constrained Quasi-Experimental Comparison of the Pre-Agentic Era (2023-2024) and the 2025 Transition

detail.title: Agentic AI, Large Language Model Methodologies, and Workflow-Level ROI in Portfolio Risk Analysis at Navy Federal Credit Union: An Evidence-Constrained Quasi-Experimental Comparison of the Pre-Agentic Era (2023-2024) and the 2025 Transition
detail.abstract: This study examines whether publicly available evidence is consistent with an improvement in the workflow-level return on investment (ROI) of portfolio risk analysis at Navy Federal Credit Union after the institution moved from bounded digital-investment automation toward a broader generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) posture. The paper deliberately avoids claiming observed client alpha, portfolio outperformance, or causal financial effects because Navy Federal does not publicly disclose member-level portfolio returns, advisory assets by workflow type, workflow-cycle times, analyst labor costs, or a standalone AI ROI figure. Instead, the study uses an evidence-constrained quasi-experimental comparison of a pre-agentic baseline period (2023–2024) and a 2025 transition period. The analysis triangulates three evidence layers: public institution-level financial indicators, observable digital-investment capability disclosures, and an Author-Constructed Agentic Portfolio Risk Capability Index (APRCI). To make the APRCI more defensible, the revised methodology provides a five-dimension codebook, score anchors, source-to-score crosswalk, equal-weighting rationale, and sensitivity checks under alternative assumptions. Results show that assets increased from USD 170.8 billion in 2023 to USD 197.2 billion in 2025, members’ equity increased from USD 14.2 billion to USD 18.9 billion, and net income increased from USD 1.37 billion to USD 1.91 billion. At the same time, the delinquency ratio rose from 1.59% to 1.96%, indicating that stronger analytics would have operated in a more risk-intensive environment rather than an artificially benign one. The APRCI increases from 48 in 2023 to 64 in 2024 and 92 in 2025, with conservative sensitivity analysis still supporting a large directional capability gain. The bounded conclusion is that the public record is consistent with improved workflow-level ROI potential through faster review preparation, richer monitoring, improved documentation, stronger explanation capacity, and more scalable human-in-the-loop governance. The magnitude of ROI remains unobserved and should be tested in future work using de-identified workflow telemetry or synthetic portfolio-review datasets.

title: Mises on Causal Regularities in Economics: Mechanisms, Tendencies and the Problem of Homo Economicus
affiliations: Nicolaus Copernicus University

detail.title: Mises on Causal Regularities in Economics: Mechanisms, Tendencies and the Problem of Homo Economicus
detail.abstract: This article addresses two apparent tensions in Ludwig von Mises's views on causality. First, although Mises maintains that theoretical economics aims to discover universal causal relationships among socioeconomic phenomena, he also claims that the sciences of human action-unlike the natural sciences-deal with the categories of means and ends rather than causality. I argue that this tension dissolves once one recognizes that Mises associates the natural sciences with Hume's regularity theory, which he rejects in economics. A second tension then arises: despite rejecting the Humean view, Mises affirms the existence of economic regularities. I argue that such regularities can be understood as tendencies generated by causal mechanisms consisting of human motives and institutions. On this interpretation, however, Mises's explicit rejection of homo economicus model renders his framework vulnerable to incoherence. I argue that the isolation of the economic motive is justified within a causal-realist interpretation of his methodology.

detail.title: Industry Rotation Using Market-State Similarity
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether lagged market returns contain useful information about subsequent industry returns and whether this information can be used for active industry rotation. Using monthly Kenneth French industry portfolios, we first show that conventional mean predictability is weak. Quantile predictive regressions, however, reveal that market-to-industry predictability is concentrated mainly in the tails of the conditional return distribution, especially in downside states. Motivated by this evidence, we propose a non-parametric strategy based on market-state similarity. At each portfolio-formation date, the strategy identifies historical months in which the standardized market excess return was closest to its current value, measures subsequent industry performance after those similar states, and goes long industries with positive historical subsequent returns and short industries with negative historical subsequent returns. Out-of-sample simulations show that the active strategy delivers a higher Sharpe ratio, lower volatility, and substantially smaller drawdowns than the passive equal-weighted industry benchmark. The results are robust to industry classification and model-parameter choices.

A Network-Capital Analysis of India's May 2026 Gold Tariff and a Markov Model of Likely Outcomes

detail.abstract: On 13 May 2026 India more than doubled its import tariff on gold and silver  from 6% to about 15%.  In an attempt to defend a rupee that had reached an all-time low of USD/INR 95.95. This paper analyses the move from a network-capital perspective, treating currencies as competing protocols rather than as units of account. The customs tariff operates on a physical commodity flow that is only weakly coupled to the protocol-switching decision that drives currency depreciation. The historical reference class is India's 2013-14 episode. It is decomposed into five contributing factors: the gold-restriction lever (trade channel) contributed approximately 0.8 of 3.1 percentage points of current-account-deficit compression, while the capital channel (FCNR(B) swap window, withholding-tax cut, 200-basis-point rate hike) contributed roughly an equal share and falling oil contributed 0.6 percentage points. A Markov transition model of the rupee's next state, conditional on the Reserve Bank of India's action and the Persian Gulf oil-supply scenario, places approximately 60% of the probability mass for the three-month horizon under the duty-only path in the bad-outcome states (severe stress and crisis). Adding the capital channel shifts that mass by approximately 20 percentage points; the full coordinated stack (duty + capital + 50-75 basis point rate response) shifts it by approximately 35 percentage points and compresses the crisis probability to under 5%. Despite a higher direct policy cost, the full stack dominates on expected-value grounds. The defence of an emerging-market currency lives in the capital channel, specifically in protocol-loyal flows from the diaspora.  Not at customs as policy signals. Tariff-based currency defence is a coordination signal, not a defence.

detail.abstract: This paper compares two machine learning architectures for intraday directional prediction in Micro E-Mini Nasdaq 100 futures (MNQ): a gradient boosting classifier operating on engineered daily and intraday features, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network processing raw five-minute bar return sequences. The comparison is motivated by recent foundation model research in financial candlestick data, including the Kronos architecture (Shi et al., 2025), which demonstrated that sequential bar-level structure contains predictive information when processed at scale. We implement a tractable approximation of this architecture adapted for a dataset of 944 trading days spanning 2021 through 2025. Four model configurations are evaluated under strict walk-forward validation with expanding training windows across three out-of-sample test periods (2023, 2024, 2025). The target variable is binary: whether the session close exceeds the 10:30 AM bar open by more than ten points. All models are evaluated against a 51.8% base rate. No configuration produces out-of-sample accuracy materially above the base rate. Combined out-of-sample accuracies range from 50.00% to 50.89% across all gradient boosting variants. The LSTM produces a combined OOS accuracy of 50.59%. Permutation test p-values are 0.135 for the best gradient boosting configuration and 0.515 for the LSTM, both failing the p < 0.05 significance threshold. Feature importance analysis across walk-forward folds reveals systematic instability: the features dominating each fold differ substantially, confirming noise fitting rather than consistent structural signal capture. We conclude that five-minute OHLCV bar sequences do not contain sufficient sequential predictive structure for session-level directional forecasting at this dataset size and resolution. The primary contribution is a documented implementation and honest evaluation of a Kronos-inspired architecture on a constrained real-world dataset, contributing an empirical lower bound on the dataset scale requirements for sequential ML-based intraday forecasting. A structural interpretation is offered: the sample size required for transformer-scale architectures to learn non-trivial financial patterns is orders of magnitude larger than what is available in four years of single-instrument intraday data.

title: The Cognitive Mirror: Between Individual Cognition and Global Crises

detail.title: The Cognitive Mirror: Between Individual Cognition and Global Crises
detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural gap between the scale of contemporary crises and the cognitive capacity of individuals to perceive and act in accordance with their consequences. Drawing on futures studies, speculative design, and political theory, it proposes a speculative artefact-a personal cognitive mirroras a reflective infrastructure: an offline, decentralized device that reveals patterns of thought and action without optimizing, recommending, or extracting. The paper develops the concept of subject-model conflict at the individual level, arguing that most existing digital systems deepen rather than resolve this conflict by designing for a rational agent that does not exist. Four speculative vignettes illustrate the three structural gaps the mirror addresses: between the scale of action and its consequences, between collective knowledge and individual access at the moment of decision, and between where causes lie and where people look for them. The paper holds open a central tension-between reflective emancipation and the capture of the reflective frame-as the most honest position available.

title: Sequential Bayesian Pricing of AI Infrastructure
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Sequential Bayesian Pricing of AI Infrastructure
detail.abstract: This paper is an exercise in assessing priors and processing Bayesian updates for asset valuation. We treat valuation as a discrete decision tree in the tradition of Raiffa and Schlaifer [1961], with terminal payoffs anchored to a contemporaneous comparable transaction and branch probabilities elicited from sector base rates. Two questions organise the analysis: what prior over states does the marginal investor hold (the inverse problem), and how should that prior update as new disclosures arrive (the Bayes factor problem)? Both admit closed-form answers under a bear-base concentration constraint. Bayes factors evolve multiplicatively along the tree: prior logodds shift by log BF t at each disclosure, and Jeffreys [1961]'s scale provides the unit of measure. Posterior uncertainty resolves at the rate ∑ t log BF t. Options markets provide a complementary identification: by Breeden and Litzenberger [1978], the second derivative of the call-price curve with respect to strike recovers the implied risk-neutral density, and around scheduled earnings disclosures this density encodes the market's prior over the announcement-induced jump. We argue this resolution-of-uncertainty calculus is under-used in finance. The framework is applied to three operators repositioning Bitcoin-mining power capacity for hyperscaler tenants, namely IREN, Cipher Digital (CIFR), and Keel Infrastructure (KEEL), anchored to Hut 8's May 6, 2026 Beacon Point lease at $27.8M per contracted megawatt. Market-implied bull-state probabilities lie an order of magnitude below subjective priors. The disagreement is in the priors, not the payoffs. The paper is methodological; worked examples illustrate the framework, not investment recommendations.

The research methodology involves the analysis of trade data from Eurostat and a comprehensive review of scientific and specialized literature. The comparative analysis is centered around categories such as cereals, vegetable oils, meat, and dairy products. Key findings indicate a significant increase in the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, especially corn, coupled with a modest rise in exports from Poland. Given the challenges stemming from the war in Ukraine, an appropriate approach to shaping agricultural policy becomes crucial for the sustainable development of the sector.

detail.abstract: This working paper studies whether decoupled ride-hailing pricing allows passenger fares and driver pay to adjust differently when local demand and traffic conditions are stressed. Using 2,292,885 zone-hour observations from New York City's 2024 High-Volume For-Hire Vehicle trip records, we combine extreme rainfall shocks with 2019 historical platform shares in a continuous-treatment dynamic event-study design. The paper links passenger fares, driver pay, quasi-take rates, passenger wait times, and neighborhood exposure within the same zone-hour framework. Areas with higher historical dominant-platform shares experience higher quasi-take rates after rainfall shocks, driven by asynchronous passenger-and driver-side price adjustment. The same areas also show longer passenger wait times, while transaction volume and inter-zonal flow proxies do not support explanations based only on demand contraction or large external supply withdrawal. We find no evidence of additional price adjustment directly targeting low-income neighborhoods. Instead, distributional exposure appears to arise mainly because lowincome neighborhoods more often overlap with areas where local competition and travel alternatives are limited.

detail.title: Selected Problems of African Agriculture and Food Production
detail.abstract: Agriculture is the dominant economic sector in Africa. Africa is distinguished by a large population working in agriculture, abundant and fertile land for self-sufficient food production, and even surplus production. However, the growth rate of food production and the ratio of those employed in agriculture to the total workforce clearly reflect the poor state of the sector. The main objective of the study is to identify the main problems and obstacles that have contributed to the underdevelopment of African agriculture from the 2010s to 2022, and to find solutions to them. The most determining factors of the continent's agriculture were collected using a PESTEL analysis. Using problem tree analysis, this paper examines the obstacles and problems that hinder the development of agriculture in Africa. It seeks answers to the problems that African governments and farmers should find solutions to in order to safely supply food to the ever-growing population. As a result, a solution tree was created. The development and modernization of agriculture in Africa is absolutely necessary to pave the way for food security and economic recovery. Self-sufficient food production would be the goal, taking into account sustainable development, which would require the identification of key policy areas, education and grassroots development of the sector, as well as curbing corruption and targeting subsidies.

detail.abstract: The global expansion of higher education is widely championed as an engine of social equity, yet the macro-structural conditions that convert educational supply into true opportunity remain debated. Leveraging the World Bank's Global Database on Intergenerational Mobility (GDIM) across 74 countries (1960s-1980s birth cohorts), this study employs a Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) framework to examine the global dynamics of educational transmission. First, we provide robust cross-national evidence of an asymmetric mobility effect: driven by the endogenous ceiling effect and rising parental baselines, quantitative expansion depresses Absolute Educational Mobility. Simultaneously, however, it substantively improves Relative Educational Mobility by weakening the determination of family origin on an offspring's relative rank. Second, we demonstrate that labor market absorptive capacity serves as a critical structural threshold. The relative equity dividend of education is strictly conditional on modern service-sector job creation; absent sufficient demand, uncoordinated expansion paradoxically exacerbates relative immobility. Third, this macrostructural matching exhibits profound gender heterogeneity. Female status attainment relies heavily on formal institutional dependence, making it acutely sensitive to the synchronization of educational supply and service-sector expansion, whereas male transmission displays historical inertia buffered by alternative resource substitution. These findings underscore that realizing educational equity dividends necessitates concurrent industrial upgrading.

Also, the research observes the persistence of inflation volatility, albeit with a mean reverting tendency. Current discussions regarding a bifurcated U.S. economy highlight the increasing economic divide between lower- and higher-income Americans in spending and earnings growth and wealth accumulation. detail.abstract: We study how new information technologies a!ect democratic decision-making in a Condorcet model with costly information acquisition. Voters endogenously choose whether to become informed. Technological change alters both information costs and signal precision, with nontrivial e!ects on equilibrium participation and collective accuracy. Lower information costs can reduce information acquisition and collective accuracy only when the electorate is odd, a phenomenon we call the oddelectorate paradox. Under uniqueness of equilibrium, however, lower costs increase participation and improve collective accuracy when initial information acquisition is su"ciently low. Improvements in signal quality need not increase equilibrium information acquisition and may even reduce collective accuracy through equilibrium responses. In large electorates, the fraction of informed voters converges to zero, while the number of informed voters converges to a Poisson distribution. Democratic accuracy may therefore rest on sparse expertise and socially aggregated information.

detail.abstract: The main objective of the article was to assess the financial resilience of agri-food companies operating in the Mazowieckie Voivodship between 2018 and 2020. An intermediate objective was additionally to assess the financial health of these entities. The study used descriptive statistics methods, ratio analysis, and Taffler's discrimination model. Empirical data were derived from annual financial statements downloaded from Dun & Bradstreet and EMIS databases. The results showed that between 2018 and 2020, most entities in the agri-food sector were doing very well and there was a low probability that their financial situation would deteriorate. It is worrying that during the period under analysis, there remained a considerable number of agri-food enterprises with a high probability of financial problems (Z-score below 0.2). This group of enterprises accounted for approximately 30% of the sample. Entities with an elevated risk of financial problems struggled with significant excess liquidity and recorded negative profitability ratios-ROS and ROA. Asset indebtedness was a factor strengthening the financial resilience of the entities under analysis. The results of the analyses can be the basis for deepening the methods for assessing resilience in the agricultural sector (e.g., as part of the CAP 2023-2027 evaluation). Future research should include, inter alia, the identification of differences in Z-score by company size or production type, as well as the identification of determinants of financial resilience in terms of other factors that have not been analyzed yet.

detail.abstract: This paper illustrates how firms with publicly disclosed political connections use subsidiaries to obtain preferential treatment in land markets. While the headquarters of politically connected listed firms pay land prices comparable to those paid by other firms, their subsidiaries receive discounts of 12.1%–13.2%. These discounts are more pronounced when land is acquired through less transparent methods, in regions with weaker institutional environments, and among private firms. The anti-corruption campaign launched in 2012 effectively mitigates corruption-related discounts, with the magnitude of the discounts negatively associated with campaign intensity. Additionally, larger discounts for subsidiaries are observed following greater charitable donations, suggesting a reciprocal relationship between firms and officials. Overall, the findings contribute to a broader understanding of how firms with publicly disclosed political ties use complex corporate structures to engage in rent-seeking behavior.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the findings of a survey on climate change risk management by Italian non-financial corporations, which was conducted by Banca d’Italia in 2024. The firm-level findings allow for a more accurate assessment of climate-related risks and of their impact on creditworthiness. The survey reveals widespread shortfalls in emission and physical risk management, transition planning, and governance. Many firms that are not insured against physical risk tend to underestimate it. detail.abstract: Excessive or inappropriate use of nitrogen fertilizers in agriculture causes environmental pollution problems around the world. The purpose of the study was to assess the state of farmers' knowledge of the regulations on the implementation of cross-compliance in terms of the implementation of the nitrate program. The empirical part of the study was drawn up on the basis of a pilot survey conducted in 2022 in the Kolno municipality. The research was carried out on a randomly selected minimum required sample of 65 respondents (farmers). The analyses of the responses presented took into account the age and education of the respondents. The relationship between the state of knowledge and education was confirmed by the chi-square test. To achieve the purpose of the study, a hypothesis was put forward, such as that farmers, although aware of the need to comply with cross-compliance, have gaps in their knowledge of the specific rules of conduct. Based on the results of the study, it was found that younger farmers showed greater knowledge of cross-compliance in the context of the nitrate program, but the best results were found in the group of younger but experienced farmers, starting from the age of 30.

Italian Abstract: L’adozione della tecnologia dei registri distribuiti (DLT), basata su blockchain, rappresenta una importante evoluzione dei processi di creazione, trasferimento e gestione di prodotti e servizi finanziari. Tra le numerose applicazioni della DLT, la tokenizzazione degli strumenti finanziari (asset tokenization) è considerata dagli operatori come una delle aree con maggior potenziale di crescita. Al fine di supportare le decisioni di politica monetaria, la vigilanza micro e macroprudenziale, la tutela della clientela e la supervisione dei sistemi di pagamento è pertanto indispensabile disporre di statistiche dettagliate e possibilmente armonizzate che consentano un adeguato monitoraggio di tali strumenti. A causa della ridotta regolamentazione a livello globale e della mancanza di sistemi centralizzati di negoziazione e regolamento, le statistiche su questi strumenti sono però ancora quantitativamente e qualitativamente non adeguate. Le banche centrali, tradizionalmente responsabili della produzione delle statistiche finanziarie ufficiali, si trovano quindi a fronteggiare una sfida impegnativa, anche alla luce della rapida evoluzione del settore. Non si può escludere il rischio concreto che le statistiche ufficiali possano progressivamente perdere traccia di informazioni rilevanti sui mercati e sugli intermediari. Prendendo spunto dalle caratteristiche del comparto delle cripto-attività, il lavoro discute gli strumenti finanziari digitalizzati, con l’obiettivo di individuare i relativi gap informativi e di delineare le linee guida di una eventuale data gaps initiative sulla materia.
English Abstract: The adoption of distributed ledger technology (DLT), based on blockchain, represents a significant evolution in the processes of creating, transferring and managing financial products and services. Among the many applications of DLT, the tokenization of financial instruments (asset tokenization) is regarded by market participants as one of the areas with the highest growth potential. In order to support monetary policy decisions, micro- and macroprudential supervision, customer protection, and payment system oversight, it is therefore essential to have detailed and preferably harmonized statistics that enable adequate monitoring of these instruments. However, due to limited global regulation and the lack of centralized trading and settlement systems, statistics on these instruments are still quantitatively and qualitatively inadequate. Central banks, traditionally responsible for producing official financial statistics, thus face a challenging task, especially in light of the sector’s rapid evolution. There is a concrete risk that official statistics may progressively lose track of relevant information about markets and intermediaries. Drawing on the characteristics of the crypto-asset sector, this paper focuses specifically on digitalized financial instruments and aims primarily to analyse the relative information gap, outlining the guidelines for a potential data gaps initiative on the topic and providing some operational suggestions to help mitigate it.

detail.abstract: Monetary policy asymmetrically affects the response of firms’ employment to an output shock and plays a role in cushioning employment adjustment over the business cycle. Combining annual firm-level data until 2020 with quarterly firm-level data until 2023 and high-frequency monetary policy surprises, we show that for a given change in output, monetary policy influences the extent to which firms hold on to labour, or “labour hoard”. Furthermore, this effect is asymmetric: a restrictive monetary policy reduces labour hoarding behaviour by 2 to 3 times more than an accommodative policy increases it. Finally, we look at the role of financing conditions and firm demographics.

detail.abstract:
Consistent reporting of supervisory information by individual credit institutions is paramount for the integrity of the data that underpins sound financial information and regulatory capital and liquidity requirements. In this context, recent findings of severe inconsistencies in sectoral attribution of credit institutions’ counterparties in key prudential reporting templates have emerged as issues warranting closer investigation. 

This paper takes a deep dive into the extent and impact of statistical mis-reporting using Large Exposure data from 2,759 credit institutions from the European Economic Area (‘EEA’), as of 31 December 2023. Under some simplifying assumptions, we quantify the scale of misclassifications and assess their impact on regulatory compliance, supervisory analysis, and capital and liquidity requirements.

The findings of this analysis reveal systemic data quality weaknesses that, if left unaddressed, have the potential to distort both public and private sector risk assessments, credit institution capital requirements and supervisory policy decisions. The findings also suggest that the identified misclassifications could only represent a lower bound for problems in the quality of prudential reporting.

The conclusions of the analysis call for increased focus on reporting practices and data integrity across the EU prudential framework.

title: Optimal Multi-Peril Insurance Coverage for a Single Asset under Asymmetric Information

detail.title: Optimal Multi-Peril Insurance Coverage for a Single Asset under Asymmetric Information
detail.abstract: A puzzle in multi-peril property insurance is that relatively observable perils sometimes receive lower coverage through deductibles, indemnity rates, or sublimits. In standard adverse-selection models with additive losses, such restrictions seem inefficient: if private information concerns another peril, the information-symmetric peril should be fully insured. This paper shows that this conclusion changes when several perils affect a single asset. When two causes damage the same house, the insurer typically does not pay two independent claims; the loss is settled under one peril-specific payment state according to a claim-attribution rule. I develop a two-peril model in which only one peril is privately informed. In the separating second-best contract, the low-risk type may optimally receive reduced coverage for both the privately informed and information-symmetric perils. Peril-specific data may lead researchers to misattribute the source of adverse selection if these settlement-rule spillovers are ignored.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the design of a blockchain-enabled Islamic finance framework for livestock asset management, intended for application across smallholder agricultural economies, with its initial executed implementation in a Mudarabah pre-pilot in rural Bangladesh. The framework combines biometric muzzle-print identification with the ZeroH platform's decentralized identity (DID) and verifiable credential (VC) infrastructure to transform unregistered cattle into digitally verifiable, insurable assets capable of serving as the basis for Shariah-compliant finance. The paper sets out a flexible business framework in which the model can be expressed through multiple Islamic finance structures; it examines a hybrid Murabaha-Mudarabah-Wakalah configuration and the modular deployment models through which the platform may be operated. It then documents the Digital Cattle Pre-Pilot, an executed Mudarabah arrangement undertaken in Bangladesh to validate the commercial and operational feasibility of a single cattle-fattening cycle. By integrating W3C-standard decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, and biometric verification, the framework addresses long-standing gaps in livestock finance (fraud, ownership verification, and regulatory compliance) and offers a design intended for replication across geographies and Islamic finance structures. The paper situates the pre-pilot within a staged impactevaluation strategy that aligns with both the Sustainable Development Goals and the Maqasid al-Shariah and that culminates in a randomized controlled trial, the established method in development economics for measuring the causal impact of technology interventions.

detail.title: Evaluation Of the Effects of Replacing the Wibor Rate by the Wiron Rate for Preferential Credits in Polish Agriculture
detail.abstract: The aim of the article is to present an assessment of the economic effects of replacing the WIBOR rate with the WIRON rate for preferential credits in Polish agriculture. The study is an in-depth case study and uses the simulation analysis method. The introduction of the WIRON 3M rate will result in a reduction in the interest rate on preferential credits granted in the future, and the nominal scale of the discount will depend on the phase of monetary policy in the country and the level of the applicable interest rates set by the National Bank of Poland (NBP). However, in the case of credits granted according to the currently applicable mechanism (interest rate based on WIBOR 3M) or the promissory note rediscount rate, the change will most likely be neutral. The largest part of the interest rate reduction in all phases of the monetary policy cycle is obtained by borrowers (farmers) using credit lines: RR (credits for investments in agriculture and inland fishing, Z (credits for the purchase of agricultural land) and most activities financed under the PR line (credits for investments in the processing of agricultural products, fish, crustaceans and molluscs, as well as the purchase of stocks and shares). In the case of disaster loans granted to insured borrowers, the only beneficiary of the index change will be the State Treasury. Quantifying the potential savings for borrowers in the agricultural sector related to changes in reference rates is not easy due to the scarcity of the available detailed data.

detail.title: Observed Appetite: A Computational Framework for Measuring Commercial Insurance Carrier Underwriting Behavior at Distribution Scale

detail.abstract: Determining which commercial insurance carriers will quote a given submission is a prerequisite to every commercial-lines placement, yet the signals available to independent agents-carrierself-reported appetite guides, application-programming-interface (API) responses from a small set of integrated carriers, and individual agent experience-have not been formalized as a computational object, nor measured against each other at scale. We call this measurement task observed appetite and distinguish it from the three established categories: stated appetite (carrier-published), API-revealed appetite (returned by integrated platforms), and verified appetite (confirmed directly with the carrier). Observed appetite is the empirical distribution of a carrier's quote-or-decline behavior computed from real submission outcomes through that carrier's own portal, partitioned by industry classification, geography, and risk size. We formalize observed appetite as a five-stage computational task (Submit → Classify → Aggregate → Score Confidence → Reconcile) with an explicit four-way ontology of appetite sources. We describe the QuoteSweep system, which implements the observation infrastructure through AI-powered browser agents operating on authenticated carrier portals without requiring API partnerships. We evaluate the stated appetite baseline against itself across a corpus of 509 commercial property and casualty (P&C) carriers. This paper presents the framework and the stated-appetite baseline; production-scale observed-appetite measurement is left to future work (§6.3). Only 2.2% of carriers publicly disclose any industry × state × size interaction, only 1.2% annotate appetite at six-digit NAICS resolution, and only 4.7% of line-of-business commitments specify a revenue threshold. When the same carrier's published PDF appetite guide and its own public appetite web page are compared at the NAICS-2 sector level (n = 189 carriers, 3,780 cells), the PDF asserts 2.14× more sector inclusions than the web page (PDF "in" marginal 33.7% vs. 15.7%; Cohen's κ = +0.25, 95% CI 0.22-0.28-fair agreement under Landis & Koch). Two surfaces of the same carrier describe systematically different coverage scopes. We release the corpus as an open dataset for reproducibility.

detail.title: A Next-Generation Deep Learning Framework to Extract Hourly Gap-Free Surface NO2 Concentrations from TEMPO NO2 Columns
detail.abstract: TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution), a geostationary satellite instrument, enables continuous daytime monitoring of NO2 over North America. Here, we develop a novel deep learning (DL) framework to extract hourly (daylight) 2×2 km2 surface NO2 concentrations from TEMPO tropospheric column density of NO2 (TrpNO2) for August 2, 2023, to December 31, 2024. First, we impute low-quality and missing pixels in TEMPO NO2 column, improving performance against Pandora from a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.40 and a percentage mean absolute bias (MABP) of 101% for low-quality pixels to R=0.69 and MABP=34%. This gap-filling step is critical, as it recovers approximately 32% of pixels in our TEMPO domain. Unlike point-based NO2 monitoring stations, our product provides gap-free surface NO2 maps across TEMPO domain, substantially enhancing NO2 monitoring capabilities. Second, we fuse gap-free TrpNO2 with in-situ NO2 observations to generate preliminary NO2 grids (”TEMPO-Fused NO2”). Third, a residual neural network (ResNet) incorporates TEMPO-Fused NO2 and other variables to generate the final gap-free surface NO2 product over the TEMPO domain. Validation against in-situ stations shows an unprecedented accuracy of DL framework at surface NO2 estimation (R=0.98, mean absolute bias (MAB)=0.81 ppb, and MABP=12.3%). The model also generalizes well spatially (R=0.95; MABP=21.4%) and remains accurate within imputed regions (R=0.97; MABP=16.5%). Despite NO2 differences between urban and rural environments, our DL framework performs strongly (R=0.93; MABP=25.3%) in rural regions when trained only on urban stations. We also provide hourly grids of NO2 estimation epistemic uncertainty to aid users in identifying pixels that require cautious interpretation.

detail.title: Spatio-Temporal Assessment of Surface Water Quality, Heavy Metal Contamination, and Health Risks from ASGM in Ghana
detail.abstract: Surface water quality in sub-Saharan Africa is being damaged by artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) but limited numbers of studies combine long-term data, quantitative health risk models and community exposure data. We examined surface water quality and human health risks in the Asutifi North District of Ghana, a river basin subject to ASGM and agriculture for the last 20 years. Water quality data (2011–2025; >2700 points) from 8 sites were analysed for WQI, Cpk, non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic health risk and using IDW and a community survey (N = 189). Four sites were classed as Unsuitable for Drinking (WQI = 215–348) and dominated by Cd and secondarily As and Pb. Of the 29 parameters monitored 19 fell below WHO/Ghana limits (Cpk < 1.00); 5 sites were in negative Cpk space (indicating a system in structural failure). The hazard index was >10 for young children in high exposure scenarios and even above 5 for 70% treatment efficiency. Total Cancer risk was >10 at every site for adults. Sensitivity analyses show contamination concentration to be the most important parameter and duration of exposure to be irrelevant due to a mathematical cancellation. Long-term, point-source pollution, indicates that remediation is needed at mine discharges rather than at the site level. This analysis provided data for emergency water supply and mine drainage treatment.

detail.title: Place and Role of Large-Scale Farms in Polish Agriculture
detail.abstract: The main aim of this study is to assess changes in the structure of farms in Poland after the political and economic transformations initiated in 1989. Changes in the structure of farms and their areas will be presented against the background of selected European Union (EU) countries. The following EU-15 countries were selected: Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands, Finland, France, Ireland, Germany, Sweden, and the United Kingdom. Of the countries that joined the EU in 2004, the selected nations were Czechia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Hungary, and in 2007, Bulgaria and Romania. In analyzing changes in the structure of farms in Poland, special attention was paid to the place and role of largescale farms. The sources of research materials were statistical data and literature. The comparative method was used in the analysis of research materials. The faster rate of increase in labor costs in the national economy and the prices of inputs for agriculture compared to the selling prices of agricultural products caused a decline in the unit profitability of agricultural production. In this situation, farmers reacted defensively by increasing the scale of production, mainly by expanding farm areas, which led to the creation of large-scale enterprises of 100 hectares or more of agricultural land. In Poland, a factor conducive to the creation of such units was the ownership transformation of state-owned farms (PGRs) caused by the political and economic changes in 1989. The current policy towards large-scale enterprises leasing State Treasury land threatens their functioning. Restricting the development possibilities of this group of enterprises is not conducive to improving the structure of farms. It threatens to reduce production and may also cause social unrest because these enterprises are significant employers in rural areas.

title: Variation Trends of Air Quality and Pollution Characteristics in Baoji City from 2017 to 2025
affiliations: Shenyang University, Shenyang University, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology, Shenyang University, Shenyang University, Shenyang University and Shenyang University

detail.title: Variation Trends of Air Quality and Pollution Characteristics in Baoji City from 2017 to 2025
detail.abstract:
The Fenwei Plain is designated as one of China's three key regions for air pollution prevention and control, characterized by complex basin topography, unfavorable meteorological dispersion conditions, and a highly concentrated industrial structure. These factors collectively result in severe particulate matter pollution in autumn and winter and increasingly prominent photochemical ozone pollution in summer.

As a sub-central city located at the western end of the Fenwei Plain and a critical node on the regional pollution transmission channel, Baoji City epitomizes the conflict between heavy industrial development and aggressive clean-energy transformation under the national "dual-carbon" goals.

To reveal the long-term evolution law of air pollution in such a representative industrial city, this study systematically analyzed the interannual variation trends, spatial differentiation characteristics, and primary pollutant transformation in Baoji from 2017 to 2025. Based on continuous monitoring data from automatic ambient air monitoring stations across four districts and eight counties, six conventional atmospheric pollutants (SO₂, NO₂, CO, O₃, PM₂.₅, and PM₁₀) were evaluated using the Spearman rank correlation coefficient method.

The results demonstrated that the overall air quality improved significantly: five pollutants exhibited significant downward trends, whereas the 90th percentile of daily maximum 8-hour average O₃ (O₃-8h) showed a fluctuating upward trend. SO₂, NO₂, CO, and O₃ have continuously met the National Grade II Standard Limit since 2020, and PM₂.₅ achieved stable compliance from 2023 to 2025.

The dominant pollution type shifted from particulate matter-dominated pollution (PM₂.₅ + PM₁₀) in 2017 to composite pollution co-dominated by O₃ and PM₂.₅ in 2025. The proportion of O₃ as the primary pollutant increased from 15% in 2017 to 28% in 2025, becoming the main factor restricting further improvement.

Spatially, PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ generally exhibited a distribution pattern with the lowest concentrations in the western mountainous areas and the highest in the central urban and eastern plain areas, with the regional concentration gradient continuously shrinking. In contrast, O₃ maintained a stable spatial pattern of high concentrations in the eastern plains and low concentrations in the southern mountainous areas, indicating prominent photochemical pollution prevention pressures in the main urban area and eastern districts.

title: Signaling Failures in Democratic Markets: Integrity, Voting Intention, and Information Asymmetry in Peru's 2026 Election
affiliations: Universidad Católica Argentina

detail.title: Signaling Failures in Democratic Markets: Integrity, Voting Intention, and Information Asymmetry in Peru's 2026 Election
detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between candidate integrity and voting intention in Peru's 2026 presidential election. Using an original dataset of 35 candidates and a self-constructed binary integrity indexbuilt from open criminal cases and inconsistencies in mandatory asset declarations (declaraciones juradas)-I find a persistent negative correlation between integrity and vote share across four data points from three distinct sourcespreliminary data, two Ipsos surveys conducted 48 hours apart, and the official ONPE results: preliminary data (ρ =-0.28), Ipsos simulated vote April 1-2 (ρ =-0.33), Ipsos final poll April 3-4 (ρ =-0.31), and official ONPE election results (ρ =-0.36). Candidates classified as low integrity received on average 4.20% of the vote versus 0.96% for high-integrity candidates-4.4 times as many votes, a gap of 3.24 percentage points. This finding survives the inclusion of controls for ideological positioning, prior political trajectory, and digital visibility (OLS, N=30, R² = 0.47). I argue this counterintuitive finding does not reflect voter indifference to integrity, but rather a fundamental signaling failure in democratic markets: voters cannot efficiently discriminate between high-and low-integrity candidates. Drawing on Akerlof's (1970) framework of markets with hidden quality, Hayek's (1945) analysis of dispersed knowledge, and Cartwright's (1999) critique of rigour without mechanism, I reframe the problem as one of information architecture rather than preferences. I conclude with a falsifiable conjecture, in the spirit of Popper (1963), that artificial intelligence designed as democratic information infrastructure can function as credible signal infrastructure, restoring the electoral relevance of integrity.

detail.title: Keeping Up at the Planet's Expense: Longitudinal Evidence on Relative Concerns and Environmental Attitudes
detail.abstract: The pressure to keep up with others may shift attention from environmental protection as a collective good toward private positional concerns. We study whether income comparisons are associated with environmental concern using the SocioEconomic Panel for 2000-2020. Individual fixed-effects linear probability models with rich reference-group definitions show that higher reference-group income is associated with a lower probability of reporting high environmental concern, while the own-income estimate is small in magnitude and statistically imprecise. A 10% increase in others' mean income corresponds to a decline of about 1-2% of the mean of environmental-protection or climate-change concern. The association is stronger among individuals with lower environmental awareness, lower patience, weaker prosocial orientation, and limited political engagement. It is also more pronounced in settings with higher pollution exposure and more intensive environmental-protection efforts, consistent with normalisation and morallicensing interpretations. The results are robust to nonlinear specifications, income-rank measures, median-based reference income, alternative comparison goods, and alternative referencegroup definitions. Overall, socioeconomic comparisons appear to be systematically related to environmental attitudes and offer policy-relevant insights for settings marked by rising inequality.

title: A Modest Legislative Proposal to Help Fix the College Football Schedule
affiliations: Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Business Law

detail.title: A Modest Legislative Proposal to Help Fix the College Football Schedule
detail.abstract:
College football coaches and administrators increasingly agree that their sport’s current calendar is “broken.” Following the recent expansion of the College Football Playoff (“CFP”) to a 12-team, championship tournament, the game’s post-season now consumes the better part of two months, stretching well into late-January. This protracted schedule has been blamed not only for distorting the competition on the field, but also for sapping fan interest and viewership from the season’s culminating matchups.

Unfortunately, no meaningful adjustment to the CFP schedule appears to be on the horizon, due in part to college officials’ desire to minimize any potential scheduling conflict with the National Football League (“NFL”). Due to an obscure statutory provision—the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 (“SBA”)—the NFL currently forgoes airing its games on Saturdays prior to the third weekend of December. This timeline has complicated the scheduling of the expanded CFP games, as college officials have sought to avoid scheduling their post-season games in direct head-to-head competition with the NFL on Saturdays in late December to the greatest extent possible.

Despite the statutory origin of this predicament, the existing discussion surrounding college football scheduling reform has largely overlooked the SBA as a potential means for fixing the sport’s calendar. Fortunately, the legislative origin of this dilemma also suggests a straightforward statutory solution. Because the SBA’s restriction preventing the NFL from playing on fall Saturdays was explicitly intended to protect college football, now that the latter’s season has crept well into January, the law should be amended to extend this protection accordingly. Such a fix would allow college officials to structure their post-season in the manner that best serves the sport, while continuing to preserve the traditional weekend dichotomy between college and professional football games throughout the sport’s full playing season.

title: Agent-Mediated Information Sharing for Anti-Money Laundering
affiliations: and Mastercard

detail.title: Agent-Mediated Information Sharing for Anti-Money Laundering
detail.abstract: Anti-money laundering investigations increasingly rely on AI-driven workflows, yet their effectiveness remains constrained by fragmented information sharing across financial institutions. While existing regulations permit collaboration, coordination in practice is largely manual and difficult to scale. This paper proposes an architecture for agent-mediated information sharing under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act, combining agent-based design principles with open agent-to-agent communication protocols. We present communication topologies-bilateral exchange, case-scoped group coordination, and open signaling with conditional session formation-that preserve institutional autonomy, enforce purpose limitation and data minimization, and enable auditable, policy-controlled exchanges of investigative context. Using a distributed money mule investigation as a motivating example, we illustrate how these topologies allow institutions to surface overlapping investigative context without centralized data pooling or expanded regulatory risk. A reference implementation of the proposed topologies is provided as a companion to this paper. To our knowledge, this is the first architectural proposal applying open agent-to-agent communication protocols to inter-institutional information sharing under Section 314(b).
